ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the riverbanks are drawn as two approximately horizontal lines, upper and lower. On the left side of the lower bank there is dock A, and on the right side there is dock B; the place on the upper bank directly opposite B is marked C, and BC is connected with a vertical dashed line, indicating the direction directly opposite. Boat A starts from near A, with its bow slanting up to the right, marked as forming 60° with the lower riverbank; boat B starts from near B, with its bow slanting up to the left, also marked as forming 60° with the lower riverbank. The problem gives AB=√3/3 H, the river width BC=H, and B can just arrive at C along vertical BC. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system, taking the x-axis along the lower riverbank from A toward B, and the y-axis perpendicular to the riverbank upward. Let the speeds of the two boats in still water both be v. Boat B's bow slants up to the left and forms 60° with the riverbank; the magnitude of the horizontal component of its still-water velocity is v cos60°, directed to the left. Its actual trajectory is just vertical BC, which shows that the horizontal velocity of the current is just to the right and cancels B's horizontal component, so the current velocity is v cos60° to the right. B's actual velocity is (0, v sin60°). Boat A's bow slants up to the right; the horizontal component of its still-water velocity is v cos60° to the right, and the vertical component is v sin60° upward. Adding the current velocity v cos60° to the right, A's actual velocity is (2v cos60°, v sin60°)=(v, v sin60°). The vertical components of velocity of A and B are the same, so the two boats are always at the same height. When they meet, A's x-coordinate must catch up from A to the vertical line where B is located, and the required time is t=AB/v=(H/√3)/v=H/(√3v). At this time the height is y=v sin60°·t=(√3/2)v·H/(√3v)=H/2. Since BC=H, the meeting point is on BC, and is H/2 from both B and C, namely the midpoint of BC.

method.method_draft: 先从图中读取结构：下岸有A、B两个码头，B的正对岸为C，虚线BC垂直河岸；甲从A出发，船头斜向右上，与河岸成60°；乙从B出发，船头斜向左上，与河岸成60°。从题文读取：河宽为H，AB=√3/3 H，两船静水速度大小相等，乙恰能沿竖直的BC到达C。建立坐标系：x轴沿下河岸从A指向B，y轴垂直河岸向对岸，设船在静水中速率为v。由乙实际轨迹为竖直BC可知，水流速度恰好抵消乙船头的水平分速度，因此水流速度大小为v cos60°且方向向右。于是乙的实际速度为(0, v sin60°)。甲的船头水平分速度向右为v cos60°，再加水流v cos60°，故甲实际速度为(2v cos60°, v sin60°)=(v, v sin60°)。甲、乙竖直分速度相同，所以始终处于同一横向高度；相遇只需甲在x方向追到B所在竖线。用AB=H/√3，t=AB/v=H/(√3v)，此时y=v sin60°·t=(√3/2)v·H/(√3v)=H/2，所以相遇点在BC上且距B、C均为H/2，即BC中点。
